summary: Becker County, MN fire tower erected 1929 as a steel Aermotor; removed in 1999 after being sold; now listed as gone.

facts.status_note: Forest Lookouts list says it was removed in 1999 after being sold; no account of the site today was found

events.note: A steel Aermotor tower was erected at Wolf Lake, per the Forest Lookouts list
Removed after being sold the previous year, per the Forest Lookouts list; the sale year is not stated

notes_for_editor: The 1929 build and 1999 removal come from one hobbyist list (Forest Lookouts), which is not a primary record. The sale year (1998) is only implied by 'the previous year' and is not stated, so no event is written for it. The agency (U.S. Forest Service) rests on one Wikipedia sentence in the Becker County article, which calls Wolf Lake the site of a USFS lookout tower; it was not checked against USFS records. The Wikipedia sentence does not put the tower on the county's high point, a hill 2.1 miles northeast of Wolf Lake. Do not use the 1955 100-foot Aermotor entry on the Forest Lookouts page: it belongs to Woodland (Kanabec County), and a search summary mixed the two up. A different Wolf Lake tower, in Lake County, Michigan (near Baldwin), is in data/raw/eastern_us_lookouts/wolf-lake.html; it is not this tower. The coordinates 46.85705, -95.35837 come from the association's list and were not checked on a map. A Star Tribune article on removed Minnesota towers was rate-limited (HTTP 429) and not read.
